questions.question_text: Which one of the following terms refers to the bias towards focussing attention on only one aspect of a situation and the inability to attend to other features?
questions.explanation: Centration is a term introduced by psychologist Jean Piaget to refer to the tendency of young children to focus attention on only one salient aspect of an object, situation, or problem at a time, to the exclusion of other potentially relevant aspects. Ref: Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. The correct answer is: Centration

questions.question_text: Which one among the following emotions arises around three years of age?
questions.explanation: The primary emotions of joy, sadness, anger, fearfulness, disgust, surprise are present within the first six months of life and develop over the next three years. However, self-conscious emotions like jealousy, shame, guilt and empathy arise later around three years. These emotions require a sense of self, a capacity that develops after 24 months. The correct answer is: Guilt

questions.question_text: Which of the following outcome can be expected from the care provided?

options.text: Cognitive recovery occurs when institutionalised children are moved to foster care
All three groups will have similar IQ profile
Age at placement under social service care has no influence on cognitive outcome
Never-institutionalised children will show lower than average IQ
Indiscriminate sociability is seen in children reared within a family system

correct_answer.text: Cognitive recovery occurs when institutionalised children are moved to foster care

correct_answers.text: Cognitive recovery occurs when institutionalised children are moved to foster care

questions.explanation: RCT of abandoned children reared in institutions vs. abandoned children placed in institutions but then moved to foster care showed markedly poor cognitive outcome for children that were in institutions; but cognitive recovery occurred significantly for younger children placed in foster care. This suggests a possible sensitive period in cognitive development. O'Connor and Rutter (2000) compared young children adopted from Romania with children adopted within the United Kingdom. They found that at both age 4 and again at age 6, the duration of deprivation was linearly related to the number of signs of attachment disorders. Children exhibiting indiscriminate sociability at age 6 had experienced deprivation for twice as long as children exhibiting no attachment disorder signs. Nelson CA III et al. Cognitive recovery in socially deprived young children: The Bucharest Early Intervention Project. Science 2007 Dec 21; 318:1937. O'Connor, T.G., and Rutter, M. (2000). Attachment disorder behaviour following early severe deprivation: Extension and longitudinal follow-up. English and Romania Adoptees Study Team. Journal of the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, 39, 703-712. The correct answer is: Cognitive recovery occurs when institutionalised children are moved to foster care

questions.question_text: Which one of the following terms describes this phenomenon?
questions.explanation: Empty nest syndrome is a depressive state that occurs in some men and women when their youngest child is about to leave home. Most parents, however, perceive the departure of the youngest child as a relief rather than stress. If no compensating activities have been developed, particularly by the mother, some parents become depressed. This is especially true of women whose predominant role in life has been mothering or of couples who decided to stay in an otherwise unhappy marriage 'for the sake of the children'. Midlife transition or crisis occurs around age 40 to 45, when individuals become acutely aware of their limitations with their previous goals and re-evaluating their life. Downshifting refers to voluntary opting out of pressurised career and giving up well-paid job for more fulfilling life (anti-urbanism). Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 911. The correct answer is: Empty nest distress

questions.question_text: All of the following terms are associated with Donald Winnicott except
questions.explanation: Object permanence is a cognitive ability associated with working memory, first identified by the psychologist Jean Piaget. This relates to a child's ability to understand that objects have an existence independent of their involvement. Infants learn to differentiate themselves from the world and maintain a mental image of an object, even when it is not visible. Ref: Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 1007. The correct answer is: Object permanence

questions.question_text: Which of the following capacity has developed in this child?
questions.explanation: Gender identity is a sense of awareness, usually beginning in infancy, continuing throughout childhood, and reaching maturity in adolescence, of being male or female, or of the experienced gender associated with one's biological sex. Ref: Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. The correct answer is: Gender identity

questions.question_text: Of all sensory systems, the system least developed at birth is
questions.explanation: Full vision develops by 6 months of age; it is the last of all senses to develop in an infant. The correct answer is: Vision

questions.question_text: Fears of rejection by peer group peaks around the age of
questions.explanation: Themes of anxiety and fears of rejection by friends initially appear by 11 to 13, peaking by 15 years and then declining by 17 years (the effect being stronger for girls than boys). The correct answer is: 15 years

questions.question_text: Superego is formed at which stage of psychosexual development?
questions.explanation: The latency stage is the stage of relative instinctual quiescence or inactivity of sexual drive during the period from the resolution of the Oedipus complex until pubescence (from about 5-6 years until about 11-13 years). Freud viewed the superego as the heir to the Oedipus complex. Children internalise parental values at about the age of 5 or 6 years. The superego then serves as an agency that provides ongoing scrutiny of a person's behaviour, thoughts, and feelings. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. pp. 1063-1064. The correct answer is: Latency stage

questions.question_text: Egocentrism is a feature of which of the following stages described by Piaget?
questions.explanation: Egocentrism is a term given a technical meaning by psychologist Jean Piaget to denote a cognitive state in which a child in the pre-operational stage of development comprehends the world only from its own point of view and is unaware that other people's points of view differ from their own. It implies a failure to differentiate subjective from objective aspects of experience, and it therefore imposes an unconscious personal bias on cognition. The classic demonstration of it is Piaget's three mountains task, in which a child sits in front of a table-top model of three mountains and is asked how the scene would look to a doll viewing it from a different angle. Most children in the pre-operational stage (children about 5 years old, for example) consistently describe the doll's viewpoint as being the same as their own. Ref: Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. The correct answer is: Preoperational stage

questions.question_text: Which one among the following was the last stage of Erik Erikson's model of psychosocial development?
questions.explanation: Erik Erikson created an original and highly influential theory of psychological development and crisis occurring in periods that extended across the entire life cycle. The last and 8th stage – integrity vs despair – takes place from about 60 years until death. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. pp. 1071-1075. The correct answer is: Integrity vs. despair

questions.question_text: In which psychiatric disorder, up to three quarters of patients report physical or sexual abuse and prolonged separation from parents in early childhood?
questions.explanation: Insecure attachment and severe trauma in childhood (such as sexual abuse) may be risk factors for borderline personality disorder. Ref: Semple D, Smyth R. Oxford handbook of psychiatry. Oxford university press; 2019 Jul 30. p. 526. The correct answer is: Borderline personality disorder

questions.question_text: In which stage of Piaget's model can a boy perceive that the amount of water present in a tall glass and a wide mouthed container is the same?
questions.explanation: According to Piaget, the stage of concrete operations lasts from about 7 to 11 years of age. In this period, children operate and act on the concrete, real, and perceivable world of objects and events. Egocentric thought is replaced by operational thought, which involves dealing with a wide array of information outside the child. Children can now see things from someone else's perspective. Children also understand the concept of conservation, which is the ability to recognise that, although the shape of objects may change, the objects still maintain or conserve other characteristics that enable them to be recognised as the same. The ability of children to understand quantity is one of Piaget's most important cognitive developmental theories. Measures of quantity include measures of substance, length, number, liquids, and area. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. pp. 1008-1009. The correct answer is: Concrete operational

questions.question_text: Which one among the following concepts is not correctly linked with its proponent?
questions.explanation: Carl Gustav Jung founded the school of analytic psychology. Jungian concepts include: Collective Unconscious: humankind's shared mythological and symbolic past is represented in the unconscious mind by archetypes (representational images of universal symbolic meaning e.g., mother, father, child, hero) Personal Unconscious: an individual's unconscious, comprising Complexes (sets of ideas and feelings triggered by interpersonal interactions) Ego: individual's conscious mind Persona: the mask covering one's personality; the face a person presents to the outside world Anima: the unconscious feminine aspect of a man Animus: the unconscious masculine aspect of a woman Shadow: a personification of the less acceptable aspects of oneself Individuation: the process in which the individual develops self-identity Extroversion (outgoing) and introversion (keeping to oneself). Ref: Semple D, Smyth R. Oxford handbook of psychiatry. Oxford university press; 2019 Jul 30. p. 888. The correct answer is: Introversion and Extroversion - Winnicott

questions.question_text: Which one of the following types of infants poorly interact with the mother and do not appear particularly upset when left with a stranger?
questions.explanation: Mary Ainsworth devised the Strange Situation procedure with 12- to 18-month infants, which categorised infant-parent relationships. The procedure involves separations and reunions with caregivers and observes response. In insecure-avoidant attachment, the child seems unconcerned at separation or reunion. It is associated with unresponsive parenting. Ref: Semple D, Smyth R. Oxford handbook of psychiatry. Oxford university press; 2019 Jul 30. pp. 658-659. The correct answer is: Insecure/anxious - avoidant infants

questions.question_text: According to Freud's psychosexual theory, Oedipus complex develops during
questions.explanation: Freud theorised that boys move through the Oedipal complex during the phallic phase (age 30-48 months to around the end of the fifth year). Ref: Semple D, Smyth R. Oxford handbook of psychiatry. Oxford university press; 2019 Jul 30. p. 894. The correct answer is: Phallic stage

questions.question_text: According to Margaret Mahler, the separation individuation phase lasts from
questions.explanation: Separation-individuation phase lasts from 5 months to 5 years of age. It is further subdivided into; a)Differentiation sub-phase: (5 to 10m) slowly appreciates the difference between mother and self b)Practicing sub-phase: (10 to18m) gradual increase in interest on the environment; practices exploration. C)Rapprochement sub-phase: (18 to 24m) Alternating drives to be autonomous and dependent; Able to explore alone but requires comfort and reassurance on return. D) Object constancy sub-phase: (2 to 5yrs) Understand that the mother will not be lost if temporarily away; hence able to function independently. The correct answer is: 5 months to 5 years

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a normal stage of grief?
questions.explanation: The classic work on stages of grief came from Erich Lindemann, who studied 101 bereaved people and published in 1944, an article titled "Symptomology and Management of Acute Grief". In this article he described a set pattern of reaction to a loss event (grief): After an unexpected death, there is an initial shock that lasts 10-14 days. After the initial shock comes a period of intense sadness, and the grieving person may withdraw from social contact. Next comes anger, as the grieving person seems to 'protest' the unexpected death. Finally, within a year or so, the grief is resolved, and the person returns to normal. The correct answer is: Protest

questions.question_text: Which one among the following is said to be achieved when all information properly fits into the schemas?
questions.explanation: In the theories of Jean Piaget and his followers, equilibration is a process of adaptation to the environment that occurs mainly through assimilation and accommodation and that tends to maintain a state of cognitive equilibrium or balance when an individual acquires new information. Ref: Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. The correct answer is: Equilibration

questions.question_text: The above reaction can be considered as
questions.explanation: Regression is a reversion to an earlier, more immature mode of thinking, feeling, or behaving. In psychoanalysis, regression is a defense mechanism whereby a person reverts to a form of behaviour, thinking, or object-relationship characteristic of an earlier stage of development in order to avoid or reduce anxiety. Ref: Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. The correct answer is: Regression

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct in this regard?

options.text: Boys are less affected than girls
Hyperactive children are more affected than easy-going children
There is no effect on cognitive development
Younger children are less affected than older children
Psychosis is the most common effect

correct_answer.text: Hyperactive children are more affected than easy-going children

correct_answers.text: Hyperactive children are more affected than easy-going children

questions.explanation: Family instability can affect children to various extent depending on sex (boys affected more than girls), age (younger affected more than older children), and temperament hyperactive affected more than placid). This has a demonstrable effect on a child's cognitive achievements; the most common psychopathology noted is a behavioural difficulty. The correct answer is: Hyperactive children are more affected than easy-going children

questions.question_text: Which of the following could be used to explain the fundamental defect?
questions.explanation: 'Theory of mind' refers to people's intuitive understanding of their own and other people's minds or mental states, including beliefs and thoughts. It develops by degrees from a very early age in humans: by the age of 3 years children normally have a well-developed theory of mind but cannot yet understand that people's beliefs can be false. This develops around 4 years of age. People with autistic spectrum disorder are severely impaired in their ability to understand mental states and to appreciate how mental states govern behaviour. Ref: Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. The correct answer is: Theory of Mind

questions.question_text: What kind of play is this?
questions.explanation: In sensorimotor play, the infant plays with objects like shaking a rattle, which occurs around six months. Symbolic or pretend play is evident by two years. Here one object is understood to stand for another (e.g. a piece of pencil stands for a cigarette) or pretending something exists where it does not (e.g. speaking to grandfather over a toy phone). The correct answer is: Symbolic play

questions.question_text: Which of the following stages in moral reasoning may not be achieved by everyone?
questions.explanation: Lawrence Kohlberg integrated Jean Piaget's concepts and described multiple stages of moral development within three significant levels of morality. The first level is pre-conventional morality, in which punishment and obedience are the determining factors. The second level is morality of conventional role-conformity, in which children try to conform to gain approval and maintain good relationships with others and are also guided by rigid codes of 'law and order' (authority orientation). The third and highest level is the morality of self-accepted moral principles (post-conventional), in which children voluntarily comply with rules based on a concept of universal ethical principles and make exceptions to rules in certain circumstances. According to Kohlberg, people vary in their moral development, that is, the ability to analyse complex moral issues. According to Kohlberg's theory, individuals who reach the postconventional level live by their own ethical principles, including basic human rights as life, liberty, and justice. They tend to pursue 'the greatest good for the greatest number of people'. Universal ethical principles may not be achieved by everyone. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 902. Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. p. 167. Fang Z et al. Post-conventional moral reasoning is associated with increased ventral striatal activity at rest and during task. Scientific reports. 2017 Aug 2;7(1):1-1. The correct answer is: Universal ethical orientation

questions.question_text: Who proposed that human beings are born with a 'Language Acquisition device' (LAD) that enables children to gather information about the rules of language use?
questions.explanation: The language acquisition device is a hypothetical mechanism, based on generative grammar, introduced by linguist and philosopher Noam Chomsky to explain how children acquire internalised knowledge of grammar with remarkable speed on the basis of fragmentary and degenerate input data. The language acquisition device is assumed to be a biologically based innate capacity for language, independent of any specific natural language, that enables a child exposed to adult speech to implement certain general principles for discovering the grammatical rules of the specific language in question. Ref: Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. The correct answer is: Noam Chomsky

questions.question_text: Which period refers to the autistic phase of Margaret Mahler's stages of child's early development?
questions.explanation: Margaret Mahler proposed a theory to describe how young children acquire a sense of identity separate from that of their mothers'. The first stage is 'normal autism' from birth to 2 months. In this stage, periods of sleep outweigh periods of arousal in a state reminiscent of intrauterine life. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. pp. 892-893. The correct answer is: 0-2 months

questions.question_text: When children are deprived of parental care from their mother or a mother substitute during infancy and in the first few years of life which of the following conditions can develop?
questions.explanation: Anaclitic depression, also known as hospitalism, was first described by Rene Spitz in infants who had made normal attachments but were then suddenly separated from their mothers for varying times and placed in institutions or hospitals. The children became depressed, withdrawn, nonresponsive, and vulnerable to physical illness, but they recovered when their mothers returned or when surrogate mothering was available. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 1013. The correct answer is: Anaclitic depression

questions.question_text: According to Thomas and Chess study, all of the following temperamental characteristics are seen in slow to warm up children except
questions.explanation: According to Chess and Thomas, children with 'slow-to-warm-up' temperament display initial withdrawal to new situations combined with slow adaptability and mild intensity. 'Difficult' children (10% of all children) display predominantly negative withdrawal responses to new stimuli, slow adaptability to change, and intense expression (fiery emotionality) of predominantly negative mood. Children with an 'easy' temperament (40% of all children) are characterised by regularity, positive response approaches to new stimuli, rapid adaptability to change, and mild or moderate predominantly positive intensity of mood. Ref: Hertzig ME. Temperament: Then and now. The Journal of nervous and mental disease. 2012 Aug 1;200(8):659-63. The correct answer is: Fiery emotionality

questions.question_text: Identify the incorrect statement about the EAS dimensions of temperament.

options.text: Temperament traits have an early onset
They show less stability over developmental periods

correct_answer.text: They show less stability over developmental periods

correct_answers.text: They show less stability over developmental periods

questions.explanation: The EAS is a developmental, multidimensional, and causal personality model described by Buss and Plomin. The acronym EAS refers to three basic dimensions: emotionality, activity, and sociability. They manifest before socialisation, persist later in life, and show substantial heritability. The dimensions of the EAS are considered stable. The initial model of Buss and Plomin featured four temperamental dimensions: emotionality, activity, sociability, and impulsivity. Purper-Ouakil D. (2017) EAS Temperament Model. In: Zeigler-Hill V., Shackelford T. (eds) Encyclopedia of Personality and Individual Differences. Springer, Cham. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-28099-8_745-1. The correct answer is: They show less stability over developmental periods

questions.question_text: The ability to formulate hypotheses and carry out deductive reasoning is a feature of
questions.explanation: According to Piaget, the stage of formal operations lasts from about 11 years of age through the end of adolescence. The stage is so named because young persons' thinking operates in a formal, highly logical, systematic, and symbolic manner. It is characterised by the ability to think abstractly, to reason deductively, and to define concepts, and also by the emergence of skills for dealing with permutations and combinations. Adolescents attempt to deal with all possible relations and hypotheses to explain data and events during this stage. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 1009. The correct answer is: Formal operational stage

questions.question_text: What are the three components of psychic functioning defined in Freud's structural theory?
questions.explanation: Freud developed the idea of distinguishing mental events on the basis of their accessibility to conscious awareness. This early, 'topographic,' theory of the mind was elaborated in 1900 in his book Interpretation of Dreams. With 'The Ego and the Id' (1923), Freud subsumed the topographic concepts of Conscious, Preconscious, and Unconscious into the 'structural' concepts of Ego, Id, and Superego. Structural Model of the Mind: Id: full of the instinctual aspects of the individual (e.g., sexual and aggressive impulses), mostly unconscious. Ego: the executive organ of the mind - linked in with reality. Superego: the seat of internalised morals and values; can be quite punishing ('thou shalt not…') or helpful in striving for a goal (the Ego Ideal). Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 1064. The correct answer is: The id, ego, and superego

questions.question_text: Which one among the following has been used as a non-verbal method of assessing children's cognitive abilities?
questions.explanation: Children's ability to draw human figures has been used as a non-verbal method of assessing children's cognitive abilities. Between 3 and 6 years of age, drawings may trace growth. A child's first drawing of a human being is a circular line with marks for the mouth, nose, and eyes; they add ears and hair later; arms and stick-like fingers appear next; and then legs appear. Last to appear is a torso in proportion to the rest of the body. Intelligent children can deal with details in their art. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 895. The correct answer is: Ability to draw human figures

questions.question_text: The scoring for Adult Attachment Interview developed by Mary Main is based on all except

options.text: The subject's ability to give a coherent account
Meaning as well as language used
The contents of the narratives provided by the interview
Security of the attachment of the subject to any specific person
The subject's ability to give an integrated account of the parenting experience

correct_answer.text: Security of the attachment of the subject to any specific person

correct_answers.text: Security of the attachment of the subject to any specific person

questions.explanation: The Adult Attachment Interview (AAI) is an hour-long, semi-structured interview about individuals' experiences with their primary caregivers during childhood. The standard coding system for the AAI focuses on the organisation and coherence of the individuals' discourse during the AAI, as these are believed to reflect individual's current mental representations ('states of mind') regarding their childhood attachment experiences. The scoring for the AAI is based on the contents of the narratives provided by the interview, the subject's ability to give a coherent account of past experiences, the subject's ability to give an integrated account of the parenting experience and the meaning as well as the language used by the subject. Ref: Raby KL et al. The latent structure of the adult attachment interview: Large sample evidence from the collaboration on attachment transmission synthesis. Development and Psychopathology. 2020 Oct 19;1:13. The correct answer is: Security of the attachment of the subject to any specific person

questions.question_text: Negative transition and risk taking behaviour are generally less common in societies that mark transition to adulthood by
questions.explanation: Initiation is a rite of passage ceremony marking entrance or acceptance into a group or society. It could also be a formal admission to adulthood in a community or one of its formal components. Risk-taking behaviour and negative transition are generally less common in such societies. The correct answer is: Initiation ceremonies

questions.question_text: According to Erik Erikson, he is at what phase of psychosocial development stage?
questions.explanation: Erik Erikson created an original and highly influential theory of psychological development and crisis occurring in periods that extended across the entire life cycle. The fifth stage (identity versus role confusion) takes place from about 13 to about 21 years of age. With the onset of puberty and its myriad social and physiologic changes, adolescents become preoccupied with identity. Failure to negotiate this stage leaves adolescents without a stable identity; they suffer from identity diffusion or role confusion, characterised by not having a sense of self and by confusion about their place in the world. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. pp. 1071-1075. The correct answer is: Identity vs role confusion

questions.question_text: Around 18 months of age, what percentage of infants have multiple attachments?
questions.explanation: By their first birthday, children do form attachments with more than one familiar figure. This includes father, siblings, grandparents and others. But it is shown that multiple attachments are the rule rather than exception. Around 18m, 87% infants have multiple attachments; 50% primarily attached to the mother, 18% to the father and the rest to equally both. Attachment process itself is more important than who the attachment figure is. The correct answer is: 87

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements about parental loss is incorrect?

options.text: Parental death has somewhat lesser impact than parental conflict and separation
Higher rates of later life depression are seen in these children
Providing day care for more than 4 months at less than 1 year age for >20hrs a week can increase insecure attachment.
Girls are affected more than boys due to parental divorce
Children who did not adapt well to may result in poor academic achievement and low self esteem

correct_answer.text: Girls are affected more than boys due to parental divorce

correct_answers.text: Girls are affected more than boys due to parental divorce

questions.explanation: Most children adapt well to parental divorce if financial support, reasonable contact with non-custodial parent and successful remarriage of single parent take place. If not, poor academic achievement, low self-esteem, 2-3 times more antisocial behaviour and higher rates of later life depression are seen. Boys are more affected than girls due to parental divorce; parental death has a somewhat lesser impact than parental conflict and separation. Providing day care for more than 4 months at less than 1 year age for and >20hrs a week can increase insecure attachment. If not, day care does not affect development adversely. The correct answer is: Girls are affected more than boys due to parental divorce

questions.question_text: During the strange situation procedure, presence of minimal distress both at separation and on reunion with the caregiver is suggestive of
questions.explanation: Mary Ainsworth devised the Strange Situation procedure with 12- to 18-month infants, which categorised infant-parent relationships. The procedure involves separations and reunions with caregivers and observes response. In insecure-avoidant attachment, the child seems unconcerned at separation or reunion. It is associated with unresponsive parenting. Ref: Semple D, Smyth R. Oxford handbook of psychiatry. Oxford university press; 2019 Jul 30. pp. 658-659. The correct answer is: Anxious/avoidant attachment

questions.question_text: Kohlberg's (1966) classic stage theory of gender development proposed that children are able to correctly identify their gender by what age?
questions.explanation: Kohlberg's (1966) classic stage theory of gender development proposed that children are able to correctly identify their gender by two years of age, understand that their gender remains stable across time by four years of age, and understand their gender to be constant and independent of external features by seven years of age. However, it is now recognised that gender identity is a multidimensional construct that includes an individual's knowledge of belonging in a gender category, experienced compatibility with that particular category, felt pressure to conform, and attitudes towards gender groups. The development of a transgender or gender nonconforming identity, for example, involves a complex interplay of phenomena over time. Fluidity and fluctuation in gender identity are being increasingly recognised. Ref: Katz-Wise SL et al. Transactional pathways of transgender identity development in transgender and gender-nonconforming youth and caregiver perspectives from the Trans Youth Family Study. International Journal of Transgenderism. 2017 Jul 3;18(3):243-63. Griffin L et al. Sex, gender and gender identity: a re-evaluation of the evidence. BJPsych Bulletin. 2021 Oct;45(5):291-9. The correct answer is: 2 years of age

questions.explanation: The EAS is a developmental, multidimensional, and causal personality model described by Buss and Plomin. The correct answer is: Attention span and persistence

questions.question_text: What percentage of patients eventually achieve level 3 post-conventional morality, described by Kohlberg's theory of moral development?
questions.explanation: Lawrence Kohlberg integrated Jean Piaget's concepts and described multiple stages of moral development within three significant levels of morality. The first level is pre-conventional morality, in which punishment and obedience are the determining factors. The second level is morality of conventional role-conformity, in which children try to conform to gain approval and maintain good relationships with others and are also guided by rigid codes of 'law and order' (authority orientation). Kohlberg's stages of moral development. Simply Psychology. https://www.simplypsychology.org/kohlberg.html. The correct answer is: 15

questions.question_text: Stranger fear peaks at
questions.explanation: Infants develop a fear of strangers when they are around 6 months of age and it peaks at around 12-18 months of age. Fear of strangers declines after the age of three years. Separation anxiety starts at 1 year of age and child shows rapproachment (hugs when coming back) by 18 months. The correct answer is: 1 year

questions.question_text: In Margaret Mahler's stages of early development, the term symbiosis refers to

options.text: Child's perception of mother and self as one unit
Child's lack of exploration of outer world
Child's ability to gratify mother's emotional needs
Child's nutritional dependence on breast milk
Child's lack of exploration of inner world

correct_answer.text: Child's perception of mother and self as one unit

correct_answers.text: Child's perception of mother and self as one unit

questions.explanation: Margaret Mahler proposed a theory to describe how young children acquire a sense of identity separate from that of their mothers'. During symbiosis (age 2-5 months), mother-infant is perceived as a single fused entity. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. pp. 892-893. The correct answer is: Child's perception of mother and self as one unit

questions.question_text: Which category of play starts around five years of age?
questions.explanation: Children's play activities are categorised according to the quality of interactions among each other. Solitary play- the child plays on its own; Parallel play-the child plays along with other children (2 years); Co-operative play-This is usually evident by 3 years and the child interacts with other children in complimentary ways like sharing, turn taking, etc; Rule- governed play - It starts around five years and the children understand the rules of games. The correct answer is: Rule- governed play

questions.question_text: Which of the following factors protects against child abuse in families?

options.text: History of childhood maltreatment in parents

questions.explanation: Protective factors against child abuse include having emotionally satisfying relationships with a network of relatives or friends. Parents who were abused as children are less likely to abuse their own children if they have resolved internal conflicts and pain related to their history of abuse and if they have an intact, stable, supportive, and nonabusive relationship with their partner. The correct answer is: Network of relatives

questions.question_text: Which of the following theories attempt to explain gender differences during development?
questions.explanation: Social learning theory is a conceptual framework that studies and explains the processes by which social influences alter people's thoughts, feelings, and behaviour. Social learning theory regards gender identity and role as a set of behaviours that are learned from the environment. Ref: Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. The correct answer is: Social learning theory

questions.question_text: She is most likely to be experiencing
questions.explanation: Despite individual variations in the bereavement process, investigators have proposed grieving process models, which include at least three partially overlapping phases or states: 1) Initial shock, disbelief, denial (minutes, days, weeks) 2) An intermediate period of acute discomfort (e.g. preoccupation, somatic distress) and social withdrawal (weeks, months) 3) A culminating period of restitution and reorganisation (months, years). Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 852. The correct answer is: Stage 2 of bereavement

questions.question_text: Which term was used by Thomas and Chess to describe the reciprocal relationship between a baby's temperament and its social environment?
questions.explanation: Chess and Thomas were among the first researchers to credit children as contributors to their own development – not as passive recipients of caregiving. They described how bi-directional transactions between children and their parents influenced each other's behaviour. The interaction between the child's temperament and the environment was conceptualised within a 'goodness of fit' framework. If there is a match between an individual's temperament and the environment, optimal development can be achieved. Conversely, poorness of fit leads to maladaptive functioning. Ref: McClowry SG et al. Temperament-based intervention: Re-examining goodness of fit. International Journal of Developmental Science. 2008 Jan 1;2(1-2):120-35. The correct answer is: Goodness of fit

questions.question_text: According to Jean Piaget's cognitive development theory, primitive self-recognition begins during
questions.explanation: In the sensorimotor stage (birth to 2 years), infants learn to differentiate themselves from the world. They also become able to maintain a mental image of an object, even when it is not visible (object permanence). At about 18 months, infants begin to develop mental symbols and to use words, a process known as symbolisation. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 1007. The correct answer is: Sensorimotor stage

questions.question_text: The attachment behaviour on display is best characterised as
questions.explanation: Mary Ainsworth devised the Strange Situation procedure with 12- to 18-month infants, which categorised infant-parent relationships. The procedure involves separations and reunions with caregivers and observes response. Bizarre, confused, or contradictory behaviour is characteristic of disorganised attachment behaviour. Ref: Semple D, Smyth R. Oxford handbook of psychiatry. Oxford university press; 2019 Jul 30. pp. 658-659. The correct answer is: Disorganised attachment behaviour

questions.question_text: Which of the following features is she exhibiting?
questions.explanation: The semiotic function emerges during the preoperational period (2 to 7 years of age). With this new ability, children can represent something else – such as an object, an event, or a conceptual scheme – with a signifier, which serves a representative function. That is, children use a symbol or sign to stand for something else. Drawing is a semiotic function. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 1008. The correct answer is: Semiotic function

questions.question_text: A child can use meaningful words without connecting words. Identify the possible age of the child.
questions.explanation: Telegraphic speech is seen where meaningful words are used without connecting words. At this stage adults interact with children in a motherese - short simple raised pitch paraphrased language directed at infants. At about 24 months, children can produce grammatically paired words and achieve vocabulary for more than 240 words. The correct answer is: 18-30 months

questions.question_text: According to Kohlberg, which stage is characterised by obedience in order to conform to the expectations of the society?

options.text: Social contract orientation of post-conventional morality
Good boy/good girl orientation of conventional morality
Ethical principle orientation of post-conventional morality

correct_answer.text: Good boy/good girl orientation of conventional morality

correct_answers.text: Good boy/good girl orientation of conventional morality

questions.explanation: The interpersonal concordance or 'good boy-nice girl' orientation is seen at conventional stage of moral development. Good behaviour is what pleases or helps others and is approved by them. There is much conformity to stereotypical images of what is majority or 'natural' behaviour approved by adults at this stage. Behaviour is frequently judged by intention -- 'he means well' becomes important for the first time. One earns approval by being 'nice'. The correct answer is: Good boy/good girl orientation of conventional morality

questions.question_text: Visual acuity reaches near adult levels by
questions.explanation: At birth, vision is the least developed of the senses, presumably because there is little opportunity for it in utero; the acuity if newborn is around 20/300. Newborns can see faces at a distance of 10 to 20 inches, the distance at which mother hold their babies. At birth, infants can track and scan objects, can discriminate levels of brightness, able to fix objects, fixed focus at about 20 cm, figure-ground discrimination. At 1 month- differentiate faces; preference shown for complex stimuli. 2 months - possesses depth perception, prefers 3 dimensional rather than 2 dimensional representations of a face. At 4 months - colour vision and accommodation. At 6 months-accurate acuity (6:6). Visual acuity reaches near adult levels by 6 months and is complete by 3 years. The correct answer is: 6 months of age

questions.question_text: In a typically developing child, babbling is seen by what age?
questions.explanation: By 6-8 weeks the child starts 'cooing'. By 6 months, a typically developing child will play at making sounds and babbles (a repeated series of sounds). Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 889. The correct answer is: 6 months

questions.question_text: The visual cliff is a test of
questions.explanation: Visual cliff is an experimental apparatus for studying depth perception in infants. It consists of a narrow wooden board laid across the middle of a sheet of heavy glass, with a chequered material immediately beneath the glass on one side of the board and several feet below it on the other side. Although the glass surface is palpably flat and solid on both sides, the chequered pattern provides a texture gradient indicating a deep cliff on one side of the central board. An infant as young as six months who is placed on the board will happily crawl across the glass to its mother on the shallow side but almost invariably refuse to cross the deep side in spite of strong coaxing and tactile evidence that the glass provides a solid surface. Ref: Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. The correct answer is: Depth perception

questions.question_text: Which one among the following terms describes this cognitive process?
questions.explanation: Transductive reasoning is the term used by psychologist Jean Piaget to denote the type of thinking characteristic of children during the pre-operational stage of development. It is so called because it focuses on concrete instances and does not follow the principle of either induction or deductive reasoning. In the pre-operational stage, children also use animistic thinking, which is the tendency to endow physical events and objects with life-like psychological attributes, such as feelings and intentions. Hypotheticodeductive thinking, the highest organisation of cognition, enables people to make a hypothesis or proposition and to test it against reality. Ref: Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. p. 777. Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. pp. 1008-1009. The correct answer is: Transductive reasoning

questions.question_text: Fear of animals comes to prominence in which of the following developmental stages?
questions.explanation: Fear of animals peaks by age 3; Fear of the dark-age 4 or 5;Fear of imaginary creatures-5 plus; Fear of open spaces arise in later childhood or adult life; Fears that arise in late childhood or adult life-fear of sex/open spaces. Teenage onwards fears of failure, illness and death emerge. Fears that show no particular age trend include fear of snakes or storms. These are normal developmental fears and not necessarily phobias. The correct answer is: Preschool children

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not considered to be a Neo-Freudian psychologist?
questions.explanation: Neo-Freudian psychologists were thinkers who agreed with the basis of Freud's psychoanalytic theory but changed and adapted the theory to incorporate their own beliefs, ideas and theories. Piaget is not usually considered as a Freudian theorist. The correct answer is: Jean Piaget

questions.question_text: The age at which Erikson's stage of industry vs. inferiority is seen:
questions.explanation: Erik Erikson created an original and highly influential theory of psychological development and crisis occurring in periods that extended across the entire life cycle. Stage 4 takes place from about 5 years to about 13 years. Its focus is industry versus inferiority. The child develops industry by learning new skills and takes pride in the things made. A child unprepared for this stage of psychosocial development, either through an insufficient resolution of previous stages or by current interference, may develop a sense of inferiority and inadequacy. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. Pp. 1071-1074. The correct answer is: 5 - 13 years

questions.question_text: which of the following might happen?

options.text: Depends on the degree of attachment

questions.explanation: Separation anxiety is seen at around age 12 months. This vignette is not about the security of attachment as children, irrespective of the degree of attachment, will show some separation anxiety. The correct answer is: 12-months-old infant will cry

questions.question_text: At what age is this game first understood and enjoyed by the child?
questions.explanation: Object permanence starts by 9 months. Object permanence is a cognitive ability associated with working memory, first identified by the psychologist Jean Piaget. This relates to a child's ability to understand that objects have an existence independent of their involvement. Infants learn to differentiate themselves from the world and maintain a mental image of an object, even when it is not visible. This ability, and the ability to perform delayed-response tasks, depends on the maturity of the prefrontal cortex: in children under about 8 months this area is not fully developed, and they perform poorly on such tasks, behaving as though 'out of sight is out of mind'. Ref: Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. p. 518. Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 1007. The correct answer is: 9 months of age

questions.question_text: Attachment behaviour typically peaks between
questions.explanation: Attachment behaviour is that displayed by the infant towards the attachment figure usually but not necessarily the mother. In the first few months, an infant orientates without discrimination, But by 5-7 months, the infant preferentially orientates and signals to discriminated persons. Separation protest is observable by 7-9 months. By 9 months, the onset of attachment and stranger anxiety could be seen. Attachment behaviour peaks between 12-18 months, and lessens by school age where the relationship is based more on abstract considerations such as affection, approval rather than on proximity maintenance. The correct answer is: 12 and 18 months of age

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a stage included in this description?
questions.explanation: Elisabeth Kubler-Ross, a psychiatrist and thanatologist, made a comprehensive and useful organisation of reactions to impending death. She proposed the following five stages: - Stage 1: Shock and denial - Stage 2: Anger - Stage 3: Bargaining - Stage 4: Depression - Stage 5: Acceptance. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. pp. 847-848. The correct answer is: Reaction formation

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct with respect to transitional objects described by Winnicott?

options.text: They reduce anxiety at times of stress
They are most important to the child during the age 6 to 9 months
Systematic parental interventions are needed to wean from transitional objects
Children never change their transitional object

correct_answer.text: They reduce anxiety at times of stress

correct_answers.text: They reduce anxiety at times of stress

questions.explanation: Winnicott developed the notion of the transitional object. Ordinarily a pacifier, blanket, or teddy bear, this object serves as a substitute for the mother during infants' efforts to separate and become independent. It provides a soothing sense of security in the absence of the mother. The security objects are generally most important when the child is about two-and-a-half years old. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 1089. The correct answer is: They reduce anxiety at times of stress

questions.question_text: How many dimensions of temperament were identified by Thomas and Chess in New York Longitudinal study?
questions.explanation: Infants vary in their autonomic reactivity and temperament. Chess and Thomas identified nine behavioural dimensions in which reliable differences among infants can be observed: activity level, distractibility, adaptability, attention span, intensity, threshold of responsiveness, quality of mood, rhythmicity, and approach/withdrawal. The New York Longitudinal Study was a thirty years (initially six years) longitudinal study of 138 children, observing childhood temperaments during their infancy and followed up at 5, 18 and 22 years. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 891. The correct answer is: Nine

questions.question_text: Which one among the following ability has been demonstrated by the Rouge Test?

options.text: Sense of self and self recognition

correct_answer.text: Sense of self and self recognition

correct_answers.text: Sense of self and self recognition

questions.explanation: In Rouge test, a spot of rouge is placed on the infant's nose, and he/she is then placed in front of a mirror. Up to the age of 24 months, children do not show self-recognition, and they appear to view the images as if it was another child. But about the age of two years, a dramatic change seems to occur. Most 24-month-old children reach for their nose, which has been demonstrated in different cultures. The correct answer is: Sense of self and self recognition

questions.question_text: In Ainsworth strange situation experiment, the child shows no preference between mother and a complete stranger. Which type of attachment behaviour is this?
questions.explanation: Mary Ainsworth devised the Strange Situation procedure with 12- to 18-month infants, which categorised infant-parent relationships. The procedure involves separations and reunions with caregivers and observes response. In insecure-avoidant attachment, the child seems unconcerned at separation or reunion. It is associated with unresponsive parenting. Ref: Semple D, Smyth R. Oxford handbook of psychiatry. Oxford university press; 2019 Jul 30. pp. 658-659. The correct answer is: Insecurely attached anxious avoidant behaviour

questions.question_text: Which one among the following terms refers to basic predispositions that underlie children's behaviour?
questions.explanation: Temperament refers to the characteristic mode of behaviour or reaction of a person. Pioneering work by Thomas and Chess conceptualised temperament as the stylistic component ('how') of behaviour as differentiated from the motivation ('why') and the content ('what') of behaviour. Ref: Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 577. The correct answer is: Temperament

questions.question_text: Which of the following is INCORRECT concerning child development?

options.text: A 2 years old child can speak more than 50 words
A child starts babbling at 3 months of age
A 4 years old child speaks with correct grammar
A 5 years old child can tell time by quarter of an hour accuracy
A 12 months old child can speak up to 3 words

correct_answer.text: A 5 years old child can tell time by quarter of an hour accuracy

correct_answers.text: A 5 years old child can tell time by quarter of an hour accuracy

questions.explanation: Reception class children (ages 4-5) begin to read the time to the hour, year 1 children (age 5-6) should be able to read the time to the hour or the half hour on analogue clocks and year 2 children (age 6-7) should be able to read the time to the hour, half hour or quarter hour on analogue clocks. The correct answer is: A 5 years old child can tell time by quarter of an hour accuracy

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not a risk factor identified by this study?
questions.explanation: According to the Cambridge study by Farrington et al, the most important childhood predictors (during age 8-10) of delinquency were antisocial child behaviour, impulsivity, low intelligence, low attainment, family criminality, poverty and poor parental child-rearing behaviour. Aggression is not a risk factor identified in this study. The correct answer is: Aggression in children

questions.question_text: Which of the following experiments is not correctly matched with Piaget's stages of cognitive development?

options.text: Classification of objects according to rules - Concrete operational stage

questions.explanation: The lack of mastery of conservation in children at the pre-operational stage was demonstrated by Jean Piaget through a series of experiments. He also used the 'three mountains task' to demonstrate that pre-operational children comprehend the world only from their own point of view and demonstrate 'egocentrism'. It is not until the stage of concrete operations that egocentric thought is replaced by operational thought. Children can now see things from someone else's perspective. Children also understand the concept of conservation, which is the ability to recognise that, although the shape of objects may change, the objects still maintain or conserve other characteristics that enable them to be recognised as the same. Ref: Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. pp. 1008-1009. The correct answer is: Conservation tasks - Sensorimotor stage

questions.question_text: Who described human infants to have an 'innate state of helplessness and would most likely perish without a caregiver'?
questions.explanation: John Bowlby studied the attachment of infants to mothers and concluded that early separation of infants from their mothers had severe negative effects on children's emotional and intellectual development. He described attachment behaviour, which develops during the first year of life, as the maintenance of physical contact between the mother and child when the child is hungry, frightened, or in distress. In his terms, the newborn infant is helpless and relies on its mother/caregiver for food and warmth and hence the attachment behaviour is essentially adaptive. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 892. The correct answer is: Bowlby

questions.question_text: The baby exhibits its first social smile at about
questions.explanation: The baby exhibits its first social smile at about six weeks. The infant starts to differentiate familiar and unfamiliar faces at three months. The correct answer is: Six weeks of age

questions.question_text: This statement refers to which one of the following ageing theories of role change?
questions.explanation: 1.Social disengagement theory: Mutual withdrawal of society and the individual occurs; increased individuality and shrinking life space are inevitable moves towards death. 2.Social (non) reengagement theory (aka activity loss theory): Ageist society reduces the social interaction that older adults can have; withdrawal is not mutual, but forced. 3.Social exchange theory: Age robs people off the ability to engage in reciprocal roles; retirement is a special social contract where productivity is exchanged for increased leisure and decreased responsibilities. 4.Socio-emotional selectivity theory: Wise investment of social energy in old age is to limit social interaction to those who are most familiar. The correct answer is: Social reengagement theory

questions.question_text: Average age of puberty in boys is
questions.explanation: Currently in UK the average age of puberty is 11-12 years in boys; slightly lower in girls. The correct answer is: 11-12 years

questions.question_text: Which of the following cognitive functions is unlikely to be affected secondary to working memory dysfunction?
questions.explanation: Executive function and its key components such as error correction are dependent on working memory. The correct answer is: Long-term recall

questions.question_text: Kohlberg's concept of conventional morality is closely related to which of the following?

options.text: A child believes that the right thing is what satisfies ones needs
A child believes that the right thing is what adults approve of
A child believes that the right thing is to uphold ethical principles
A child believes that the right thing is one that avoids punishments
A child believes that the right thing is what the intuition suggests

correct_answer.text: A child believes that the right thing is what adults approve of

correct_answers.text: A child believes that the right thing is what adults approve of

questions.explanation: Lawrence Kohlberg integrated Jean Piaget's concepts and described multiple stages of moral development within three significant levels of morality. The first level is pre-conventional morality, in which punishment and obedience are the determining factors. The second level is morality of conventional role-conformity, in which children try to conform to gain approval and maintain good relationships with others and are also guided by rigid codes of 'law and order' (authority orientation). The third and highest level is the morality of self-accepted moral principles (post-conventional), in which children voluntarily comply with rules based on a concept of universal ethical principles and make exceptions to rules in certain circumstances. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 902. Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. p. 167. The correct answer is: A child believes that the right thing is what adults approve of

questions.question_text: By what age is this milestone generally achieved?
questions.explanation: Cooing- 2months; Babbling (gaga, dada)- 6 months (4 to10 months); One-word stage (mamma, doggie)- 1 year (10 to18 months); Two word stage (mummy go, daddy go)- 2 years (18 to 24 months); Basic adult grammatical sentence- 3 years; Adult speech- 5 years. The correct answer is: 5 years

questions.question_text: Her temperament is best termed as
questions.explanation: According to Chess and Thomas, children with 'slow-to-warm-up' temperament display initial withdrawal to new situations combined with slow adaptability and mild intensity. 'Difficult' children (10% of all children) display predominantly negative withdrawal responses to new stimuli, slow adaptability to change, and intense expression of predominantly negative mood. Children with an 'easy' temperament (40% of all children) are characterised by regularity, positive response approaches to new stimuli, rapid adaptability to change, and mild or moderate predominantly positive intensity of mood. Ref: Hertzig ME. Temperament: Then and now. The Journal of nervous and mental disease. 2012 Aug 1;200(8):659-63. The correct answer is: Easy

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a feature of Piaget's sensorimotor stage?
questions.explanation: In the pre-operational stage, children use animistic thinking, which is the tendency to endow physical events and objects with life-like psychological attributes, such as feelings and intentions. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 1008. The correct answer is: Animism

questions.question_text: This is seen in which of the following stages described by Mahler?
questions.explanation: Margaret Mahler proposed a theory to describe how young children acquire a sense of identity separate from that of their mothers'. During symbiosis (age 2-5 months), mother-infant is perceived as a single fused entity. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. pp. 892-893. The correct answer is: Symbiosis phase

questions.question_text: In Piaget's theory of cognitive development, the process of solving new problems using existing schemata is termed as
questions.explanation: In the writings of psychologist Jean Piaget, assimilation is a form of adaptation in which novel experiences are incorporated into existing psychological structures or processes, as when an infant responds to a new toy that is introduced into its environment by treating it like an already familiar object, interpreting it on the basis of past experience as something to be grasped, shaken, put in the mouth, and so on. According to Piaget, accommodation is also a form of adaptation, but it is different from assimilation in that psychological structures or processes are modified to fit the changing demands of the environment. Ref: Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. The correct answer is: Assimilation

questions.question_text: Based on this finding, identify the category of adult attachment:
questions.explanation: The Adult Attachment Interview (AAI) – an hour-long, semi-structured interview about individuals' experiences with their primary caregivers during childhood – is a widely used measure in both developmental science and developmental psychology research for assessing adults' attachment representations. The standard system for coding the AAI recommends classifying individuals categorically as having an autonomous, dismissing, preoccupied/entangled, or unresolved/disorganised attachment state of mind. Individuals who become emotionally overwhelmed when discussing childhood caregiving experiences are classified as having a preoccupied or entangled state of mind. Ref: Raby KL et al. The latent structure of the adult attachment interview: Large sample evidence from the collaboration on attachment transmission synthesis. Development and Psychopathology. 2020 Oct 19;1:13. The correct answer is: Preoccupied/entangled

questions.question_text: Which stage of language development is he at?
questions.explanation: This is called as two words / telegraphic speech stage. In telegraphic speech, meaningful words are used without connecting words such as propositions or conjunctions. The correct answer is: Telegraphic period

questions.question_text: In Harlow's rhesus monkey studies, orphaned baby monkeys show a preference for clinging to a

options.text: Wire mesh surrogate mother that does not dispenses milk
Wire mesh surrogate mother irrespective of feeding
Wire mesh surrogate mother that dispenses milk
Soft cloth surrogate mother that provides food
Soft cloth surrogate mother irrespective of feeding

correct_answer.text: Soft cloth surrogate mother irrespective of feeding

correct_answers.text: Soft cloth surrogate mother irrespective of feeding

questions.explanation: In a series of experiments, Harry Harlow separated rhesus monkeys from their mothers during their first weeks of life. During this time, the monkey infant depends on its mother for nourishment and protection, and physical warmth and emotional security – 'contact comfort', as Harlow first termed it. Harlow substituted a surrogate mother made from wire or cloth for the real mother. The infants preferred the cloth-covered surrogate mother, that provided contact comfort, to the wire surrogate, which provided food but no contact comfort. The terry-cloth soft-surrogate mother was preferred even if it did not have a feeding nipple attached to it. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 1043. The correct answer is: Soft cloth surrogate mother irrespective of feeding

questions.question_text: According to Vygotsky's developmental theory which one among the following refers to functions that are not yet fully achieved but are in the process "pipeline"?
questions.explanation: According to Vygotsky's theory development is not entirely private or individual-based. A child acts as an apprentice in social surroundings rather than as a scientist. Parents and teachers carry out the role of scaffolding (a term introduced by Wood et al. 1976) which serves to introduce familiarity for tasks, even if those tasks are beyond a child's immediate expertise, so that the child can develop its own comptence later (collaborative learning). Zone of proximal development refers to functions which are not yet fully achieved but are in the process 'pipeline'. While actual achievement measures development after completion retrospectively, the zone of proximal development has a prospective sense as to what the child will be achieving in the near future. The correct answer is: Zone of proximal development

questions.question_text: This statement refers to
questions.explanation: Repression is a defense mechanism whereby unacceptable thoughts, feelings, or wishes are banished from consciousness. It is characterised by the unconscious forgetting of ideas or impulses in order to protect the psyche. Ref: Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. Casey P, Kelly B. Fish's clinical pathology: Signs and symptoms in psychiatry, 4th Edition. 2019. p. 130. The correct answer is: Repression

questions.question_text: Castration anxiety is associated with which stage of psychosexual development?
questions.explanation: Freud theorised that boys move through the Oedipal complex during the phallic phase (age 30-48 months to around the end of the fifth year). The castration complex is closely linked with the Oedipus complex, focusing on the fantasy of one's penis being cut off, evoked in a child by the discovery of the anatomical difference between the sexes. Ref: Semple D, Smyth R. Oxford handbook of psychiatry. Oxford university press; 2019 Jul 30. p. 894. Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. The correct answer is: Phallic stage

questions.question_text: In Piaget's theory of cognitive development, the concrete operational stage lasts from
questions.explanation: According to Piaget, the stage of concrete operations lasts from about 7 to 11 years of age. In this period, children operate and act on the concrete, real, and perceivable world of objects and events. Egocentric thought is replaced by operational thought, which involves dealing with a wide array of information outside the child. Children can now see things from someone else's perspective. Children also understand the concept of conservation, which is the ability to recognise that, although the shape of objects may change, the objects still maintain or conserve other characteristics that enable them to be recognised as the same. The ability of children to understand quantity is one of Piaget's most important cognitive developmental theories. Measures of quantity include measures of substance, length, number, liquids, and area. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. pp. 1008-1009. The correct answer is: 7 to 12 years

questions.question_text: What type of attachment is seen here?
questions.explanation: Mary Ainsworth devised the Strange Situation procedure with 12- to 18-month infants, which categorised infant-parent relationships. The procedure involves separations and reunions with caregivers and observes response. In insecure (anxious)-avoidant attachment, the child seems unconcerned at separation or reunion. It is associated with unresponsive parenting. Ref: Semple D, Smyth R. Oxford handbook of psychiatry. Oxford university press; 2019 Jul 30. pp. 658-659. The correct answer is: Anxious avoidant attachment

questions.question_text: Choose the correct statement about Bowlby's attachment theory?

options.text: Attachment behaviour will cease if there is frequent punishment from attachment figure
According to attachment theory, multiple attachments cannot occur
The primary attachment figure is not necessarily the mother
Attachment behaviour is least evident when the infant is stressed

correct_answer.text: The primary attachment figure is not necessarily the mother

correct_answers.text: The primary attachment figure is not necessarily the mother

questions.explanation: Attachment theory originated in the work of John Bowlby. Being monotropic, infants tend to attach to one person, but they can form attachments to several people. A basic sense of security and safety is derived from a continuous and close relationship with a caregiver. Abused children often maintain their attachments to abusive parents. When children are rejected by their parents or are afraid of them, their attachment may increase. The applications of attachment theory in psychotherapy are numerous. When a patient can attach to a therapist, a secure base effect is seen. The patient may then be able to take risks, mask anxiety, and practice new patterns of behaviour that otherwise might not have been attempted. Patients whose impairments can be traced to never having made an attachment in early life may do so for the first time in therapy. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. pp. 1011-1013. The correct answer is: The primary attachment figure is not necessarily the mother

questions.question_text: Which of the following models divide the mind into unconscious, preconscious and conscious?
questions.explanation: In psychoanalysis, the topographic model outlined by Freud is a description of the layout of the mental apparatus in terms of the unconscious, preconscious, and conscious. This early theory of the mind was elaborated in the 1900 Interpretation of Dreams. Ref: Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. The correct answer is: Topographic

questions.question_text: Imprinting is characterised by
questions.explanation: Imprinting is a form of rapid learning that takes place during a critical period of development immediately or shortly after birth and is extremely resistant to extinction, the most familiar example being the behaviour of newly hatched ducklings that become imprinted on, and subsequently follow around, virtually any moving object to which they are exposed during the critical period following hatching. Imprinting was first studied in detail by the zoologist Konrad Lorenz. Imprinting is characterised by irreversibility, sensitive period, specificity and life-long retention. Ref: Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. The correct answer is: All of the listed options

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements about attachment theory is not true?

options.text: Children can be attached as strongly to the father as the mother
According to attachment theory, multiple attachments can occur
Attachment behaviour is most evident when the infant is stressed
Attachment can develop despite frequent punishment from attachment figure
