questions.question_text: This parenting style is called
questions.explanation: This is called as permissive parenting with low or absent control but high degree of nurturance and leniency; No demands are placed on growing child. There is a degree of inadequate communication in these families. The correct answer is: Permissive parenting

questions.question_text: In terms of Mahler's separation-individuation theory, this infant is in the stage of
questions.explanation: Margaret Mahler proposed a theory to describe how young children acquire a sense of identity separate from that of their mothers'. The stage of rapprochement occurs from 18-24 months of age. As children slowly realise their helplessness and dependence, the need for independence alternates with the need for closeness. Children move away from their mothers and come back for reassurance. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. pp. 892-893. The correct answer is: rapprochement

questions.question_text: Mahler is associated with
questions.explanation: Margaret Mahler proposed a theory to describe how young children acquire a sense of identity separate from that of their mothers'. The first stage is 'normal autism' from birth to 2 months. In this stage, periods of sleep outweigh periods of arousal in a state reminiscent of intrauterine life. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. pp. 892-893. The correct answer is: Autistic phase

questions.question_text: Who was the most important person in the following list to be associated with the object relations theory?
questions.explanation: In psychoanalysis, object relations refer to the emotional bonds that people form with instinctual objects, in contra-distinction to interest in and love of oneself. It is given expression through capacity to form loving relationships with other people, any such bond being called an object-relationship. The concept is associated with the work of the psychoanalyst Melanie Klein and her followers. Ref: Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. The correct answer is: Melanie Klein

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a feature of restricted language code?

options.text: It is used by the middle class and upper-class children
Restricted language code is characterised by short, incomplete sentences, which focuses on the present
I is frequently employed in the restricted language code
It is characterized by longer, complex sentences that are context-independent
It focuses on the past and future, employs 'I' commonly and allows for expression of abstract thought.

correct_answer.text: Restricted language code is characterised by short, incomplete sentences, which focuses on the present

correct_answers.text: Restricted language code is characterised by short, incomplete sentences, which focuses on the present

questions.explanation: The elaborated code is characterized by longer, complex sentences that are context-independent. It focuses on the past and future, employs 'I' commonly and allows for the expression of abstract thought. Restricted language code is characterised by short, incomplete sentences, which tend to be context-dependent, frequently uses like 'you know', focuses on the present, employs pronoun I rarely and has little room for expressing abstract thinking. Restricted code is used by the poorer class and the elaborated language code is used by the middle class and upper-class children. The correct answer is: Restricted language code is characterised by short, incomplete sentences, which focuses on the present

questions.question_text: According to Erik Erikson, he's at what stage of psychosocial development?
questions.explanation: Erik Erikson created an original and highly influential theory of psychological development and crisis occurring in periods that extended across the entire life cycle. Stage 4 takes place from about 5 years to about 13 years. Its focus is industry versus inferiority. The child develops industry by learning new skills and takes pride in the things made. A child unprepared for this stage of psychosocial development, either through an insufficient resolution of previous stages or by current interference, may develop a sense of inferiority and inadequacy. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. pp. 1071-1074. The correct answer is: Industry vs. inferiority

questions.question_text: The parallel process in a female child that resembles the Oedipus complex in males is called
questions.explanation: In analytical psychology, the Electra complex is the female Oedipus complex. The term was introduced by Carl Jung and is named after Electra in Greek mythology who arranged for the murder of her mother, who in turn had murdered Electra's father. Ref: Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. The correct answer is: Electra complex

questions.question_text: Which one of the following fears is not characteristic of infancy?
questions.explanation: Stimuli that alarm infants and cause fear include loud noises, falling, and cold blasts of air. Separation anxiety is the response of an infant who is isolated or separated from its mother or caretaker. It is most common at 10-18 months of age. Somewhat earlier (at about 8 months) stranger anxiety, an anxiety response to someone other than the caregiver, appears. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. pp. 1012-1013. The correct answer is: Fear of the dark

questions.question_text: Children adopted before what age do well in terms of attachment patterns?
questions.explanation: Research shows that the earlier the age of adoption, the better is the outcome for the child. When a child is adopted during early childhood, then the chances of forming new attachments are better. Therefore, early adoption is recommended as a matter of social policy. Children adopted before the age of 4 or 5 have been shown to do well generally. Although late adoption after the age of eight, does not necessarily lead to problems in adjustment, such children are more vulnerable and are at risk of developing future problems, like behavioural problems at home and school (Tizard and Hodges 1978). The correct answer is: Four or five years

questions.question_text: Language is slower to develop in
questions.explanation: Language is slower to develop in boys, in twins, in larger families, in those from social classes 4 and 5 and in children with a lack of stimulation e.g. deaf and neglected children. The correct answer is: All of the listed options

questions.question_text: The best possible course of action is

options.text: Schedule the child for detailed psychiatric evaluation
Examine for signs of physical abuse
Reassure the parents about age-related behaviour

correct_answer.text: Reassure the parents about age-related behaviour

correct_answers.text: Reassure the parents about age-related behaviour

questions.explanation: Imaginary companions most often appear during preschool years, usually in the form of persons. They may also be things, such as anthropomorphised toys. Some studies indicate that up to 50% of children between the ages of 3 and 10 years have imaginary companions at one time or another. Their significance is not clear, but these figures are usually friendly, relieve loneliness, and reduce anxiety. In most instances, imaginary companions disappear by age 12, but they can occasionally persist into adulthood. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 895. The correct answer is: Reassure the parents about age-related behaviour

questions.question_text: The most common type of attachment behaviour in the Western world is
questions.explanation: 60-70% of children are securely attached. 15-20% show insecure-avoidant attachment. 10-15% show insecure-ambivalent attachment. 5-10% are disorganised in their attachment style. Ref: Semple D, Smyth R. Oxford handbook of psychiatry. Oxford university press; 2019 Jul 30. p. 659. The correct answer is: Secure

questions.question_text: According to the Social Learning Theory which of the following plays no role in the development of gender appropriate behaviours?
questions.explanation: The Social Learning Theory was proposed by Bandura as a way of explaining how children acquire their gender identity based on the influence of other people (particularly their parents). http://scienceaid.co.uk/psychology/gender/learning.html. The correct answer is: Archetypal schema

Imprinting was first studied in detail by the zoologist Konrad Lorenz. Ref: Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. The correct answer is: Imprinting

questions.question_text: In the above scenario, the psychosexual developmental stage of the child is most likely to be
questions.explanation: At age 7, the latent stage is more likely to be present. The correct answer is: Latent stage

questions.question_text: Insecure attachment during early childhood is associated with the development of which types of childhood disorders?
questions.explanation: Secure attachment appears to be a protective factor for development of childhood disorders and insecure attachment is best conceptualised as a risk factor for a number of childhood disorders. It has been demonstrated in various studies that insecure attachment during early childhood is associated with the development of behavioural problems especially oppositional defiant disorder at school age. Insecure attachment in combination with other vulnerability factors such as family dysfunction, difficult child temperament, and poor parental management can give rise to later childhood disorders. The correct answer is: Oppositional defiant disorder

questions.question_text: Which among the following feature is demonstrated in this 'mountain task' experiment?
questions.explanation: Egocentrism is a feature of pre operational stage (2-7 years). This does not refer to self-centeredness or selfish attitude. It refers to the restrictive ability of viewing the world from a single point of view at this developmental stage. In the famous mountain task, the child is presented with a model of mountain scene consisting of three mountains and asked what an observer would see from a vantage point different from that of the child. This is usually carried out by placing a doll in different positions and getting the child to describe what the doll would be able to see (e.g. cows, horses, etc. that are placed on the surface). Typically children under the age of eight assume that others share their view point and find it impossible to take a perspective different from their own. The correct answer is: Egocentrism

questions.question_text: Precocious puberty is suspected in girls before the age of
questions.explanation: Precocious puberty is suspected in boys before age 9, and girls before age 8. Social stress is a puberty accelerator, with familial disruption and father absenteeism, being one of the most effective stressors. In UK the average age of onset of puberty in males is 11.2 years; for females it is 11 years. Menarche on average is at 12.5 years for females. There has been a decline in western countries in the age of menarche over the last century from 16 in the 1860s to around 13 in the 1960s. This secular trend is thought to be due to the improved nutritional status of the society in general. The correct answer is: 8

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT an effect of parental separation?

options.text: Guilt and accepting responsibility for separation

questions.explanation: Children of all age groups are prone to behavioural difficulties after parental divorce -this is evident even in infants who may show changes in eating, sleeping and bowel patterns, with fearful or anxious responses. Academic and social aptitude suffers due to divorce; asthma, injuries, headaches and speech defects are more common in divorced families. The correct answer is: Increased motivation for academic performance

questions.question_text: Winnicott called these objects
questions.explanation: Winnicott developed the notion of the transitional object. Ordinarily a pacifier, blanket, or teddy bear, this object serves as a substitute for the mother during infants' efforts to separate and become independent. It provides a soothing sense of security in the absence of the mother. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 1089. The correct answer is: Transitional objects

questions.question_text: The basis of object relations theory is that the primary motivational drive of an individual is to seek
questions.explanation: In psychoanalysis, object relations refer to the emotional bonds that people form with instinctual objects, in contra-distinction to interest in and love of oneself. It is given expression through capacity to form loving relationships with other people, any such bond being called an object-relationship. The concept is associated with the work of the psychoanalyst Melanie Klein and her followers. Ref: Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. The correct answer is: Relationships

questions.question_text: Klein's depressive position is related to the process of learning to cope with which of the following conflicts?
questions.explanation: Through her study of early life and children's play, Melanie Klein proposed that aggressive and destructive forces were central components of early development. She described two positions - paranoid-schizoid position and depressive position. Paranoid-schizoid position: infants' mode of organising experience in which all aspects of infant and mother are split into good and bad elements (idealized or denigrated). Depressive position: once able to integrate good and bad, infants become concerned that they may have harmed or destroyed the mother through hostile and sadistic fantasies; the mother is viewed ambivalently as having both positive and negative aspects, and as the target of a mixture of loving and hateful feelings. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 1083. The correct answer is: Ambivalence

questions.question_text: Within the theory of mind, the ability to conceptualise false beliefs develops around
questions.explanation: 'Theory of mind' refers to people's intuitive understanding of their own and other people's minds or mental states, including beliefs and thoughts. It develops by degrees from a very early age in humans: by the age of 3 years children normally have a well-developed theory of mind but cannot yet understand that people's beliefs can be false. This develops around 4 years of age. Ref: Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. The correct answer is: 4 years of age

questions.question_text: Which one of the following attachment category has not been described in the adult attachment interview developed by Mary Main?
questions.explanation: The Adult Attachment Interview (AAI) – an hour-long, semi-structured interview about individuals' experiences with their primary caregivers during childhood – is a widely used measure in both developmental science and developmental psychology research for assessing adults' attachment representations. The standard system for coding the AAI recommends classifying individuals categorically as having an autonomous, dismissing, preoccupied/entangled, or unresolved/disorganised attachment state of mind. Ref: Raby KL et al. The latent structure of the adult attachment interview: Large sample evidence from the collaboration on attachment transmission synthesis. Development and Psychopathology. 2020 Oct 19;1:13. The correct answer is: Autocratic

questions.question_text: Following separation from the mother, the first reaction exhibited by a child is most likely to be
questions.explanation: Acute separation reaction occurs when a child is separated from their attachment figure and is sometimes called anaclitic depression. It progresses through classic stages of protest, despair and detachment. The correct answer is: Protest

questions.question_text: Which stage of moral development is he exhibiting?
questions.explanation: Lawrence Kohlberg integrated Jean Piaget's concepts and described multiple stages of moral development within three significant levels of morality. The first level is pre-conventional morality, in which punishment and obedience are the determining factors. The second level is morality of conventional role-conformity, in which children try to conform to gain approval and maintain good relationships with others and are also guided by rigid codes of 'law and order' (authority orientation). The third and highest level is the morality of self-accepted moral principles (post-conventional), in which children voluntarily comply with rules based on a concept of universal ethical principles and make exceptions to rules in certain circumstances. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 902. Colman AM. Oxford Dictionary of Psychology, 4th Edition. 2015. p. 167. The correct answer is: Pre-conventional stage

questions.question_text: What term was used by Bowlby to describe this tendency?
questions.explanation: Attachment theory originated in the work of John Bowlby. Being monotropic, infants tend to attach to one person, but they can form attachments to several people. A basic sense of security and safety is derived from a continuous and close relationship with a caregiver, usually the mother. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 1011. The correct answer is: Monotropy

questions.question_text: According to Thomas and Chess study, what percentage of children are considered to be 'difficult'?
questions.explanation: According to Chess and Thomas, children with 'slow-to-warm-up' temperament display initial withdrawal to new situations combined with slow adaptability and mild intensity. 'Difficult' children (10% of all children) display predominantly negative withdrawal responses to new stimuli, slow adaptability to change, and intense expression of predominantly negative mood. Children with an 'easy' temperament (40% of all children) are characterised by regularity, positive response approaches to new stimuli, rapid adaptability to change, and mild or moderate predominantly positive intensity of mood. Ref: Hertzig ME. Temperament: Then and now. The Journal of nervous and mental disease. 2012 Aug 1;200(8):659-63. The correct answer is: 10%

questions.question_text: What is the most sensitive period for development of attachment behaviour in human beings?
questions.explanation: According to Bowlby, attachment develops in the latter part of infancy, in the period from six to eighteen months. Attachment behaviour peaks between 12-18 months. After this period, the attachment gets stabilized, and disruption of the bond is likely to lead to deleterious effects. Although infancy may be the optimal time to develop attachment, it has been shown that children adopted at four years are also capable of developing last lasting attachment to their adoptive parents (Tizard and Hodges 1978). The correct answer is: 6 to 18 months

questions.question_text: Failure to develop attachment can lead to affectionless psychopathy and developmental retardation according to Rutter. The term used to describe this adverse outcome is
questions.explanation: Michael Rutter distinguished deprivation from privation. He argued that if a child fails to develop an attachment this is privation, whereas deprivation refers to the loss of or damage to an attachment. From his research on privation, Rutter proposed that as the child matures, he shows an inability to keep rules, form lasting relationships, or feel guilt. He also found evidence of antisocial behaviour, affectionless psychopathy, and disorders of intellectual development. Ref: McLeod, S. A. (2008, February 05). Privation and attachment. Simply Psychology. https://www.simplypsychology.org/privation.html. The correct answer is: Privation

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not a feature of 'ex-institutional syndrome'?

options.text: They were less likely to be selective in choosing their friends
They turned to peers less often for emotional support
These young people related better to adults than to their peers
It is defined in adopted children at the age of eight
They were less likely to have a special friend

correct_answer.text: It is defined in adopted children at the age of eight

correct_answers.text: It is defined in adopted children at the age of eight

questions.explanation: Tizard and Hodges followed up a group of children who had been in institutions from infancy, adopted at age 4 and had been looked after by a number of carers who often changed. At age 8, most children had formed a reasonably good attachment with their adoptive parents. At age 16, although the adolescents appeared to be functioning rather well, they showed a constellation of features termed as an Ex-institutional syndrome. These young people related better to adults than to their peers, were less likely to have a special friend, were less likely to be selective in choosing their friends and turned to peers less often for emotional support. The correct answer is: It is defined in adopted children at the age of eight

questions.question_text: The strange situation procedure is designed for use with children between the ages of
questions.explanation: Mary Ainsworth devised the Strange Situation procedure with 12- to 18-month infants, which categorised infant-parent relationships. The procedure involves separations and reunions with caregivers and observes response. Ref: Semple D, Smyth R. Oxford handbook of psychiatry. Oxford university press; 2019 Jul 30. p. 658. The correct answer is: 1 year and 18 months

questions.question_text: Who developed the theory of good-enough mothering?
questions.explanation: Donald Winnicott believed that the mother need not be perfect, but she must provide 'good-enough mothering'. The mother plays a vital role in bringing the world to the child and offering empathetic anticipation of the infant's needs. If the mother can resonate with the infant's needs, the baby can become attuned to its bodily functions and drives that are the basis for the gradually evolving sense of self. Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 893. The correct answer is: Winnicott
